title: 农业扩张
prompt:
Edit the provided miniature planet into a later stage of THE SAME civilization-management game. Preserve its exact low-poly aesthetic, camera, full-globe composition, overall coastline, single lower-left calm bay, upper-left forest reserve and upper-right rocky hill. It should be recognizably the same planet after the player has developed it. Keep the full sphere visible. Bright faceted low-poly geometry, natural jade greens, warm ochre roofs, light-blue empty background, soft sunlight. Keep facilities useful and readable, with functional props and connected roads. All buildings align to local spherical ground. No isolated ornamental cottages, no purposeless roads, no hero, no direct-control character. Small citizens and vehicles are autonomous background workers. Do not cover the whole planet in construction; retain forest resources and a meaningful open buildable area.

Water design is deliberately feasible for a game: continuous calm blue water shell at a fixed level, a clean fixed shoreline, only a few long soft pale streaks to suggest slowly scrolling texture. No waterfalls, no cascade, no splashes, no elaborate animated foam, no breaking waves, no rivers cutting across steep mountains. Shoreline water must never fall down cliffs or spill off the sphere. A short shallow irrigation channel may be used only where explicitly requested below, running along a gentle contour with visible fixed channel borders.

Render WORLD ART ONLY. No interface, no text, no captions, no arrows, no labels, no badges, no typography, no giant holograms. We will add precise management UI and explanations separately. Every new building must have a clear function and recognizable tools or stored materials. No spaceships, no off-planet content, no satellites, no huge skyline. No vague futuristic monoliths. The development state is specified below.

STAGE 2: AGRICULTURE AND GROWTH. Keep the logging camp at the upper-left forest edge, the stone quarry at the upper-right hill foot, the central stockpile, and the existing housing location.

Develop the open grassy land just below and to the right of the central stockpile into THREE orderly cultivated plots, one golden wheat field and two green crop fields. Put a modest unmistakable timber granary with grain sacks directly BETWEEN these fields and the central store, reached by one short dirt road. A small practical TOOL WORKSHOP, an open-sided wooden shed with a workbench, axe heads and wooden handles, sits immediately right of the store and close to the stone and timber delivery path. Expand the existing two-hut housing group to FOUR compact thatched or simple wood houses only in the same small north-central residential cluster. Do not scatter housing around the globe.

Make the player choice readable: farms and granary support population growth; the tool workshop improves gathering and construction. Visible stored grain and tools emphasize their different functions. Retain a small berry patch as a basic fallback food source. One modest shallow timber-lined IRRIGATION DITCH starts at a simple intake at the calm bay edge and follows a short gentle contour to the nearest cultivated plot. It has a plain blue ribbon surface and only two or three pale lengthwise flow streaks. This is a cheap fixed-shape water channel, no splash or waterfall, no network of complex rivers, no waterwheel and no dam. Show one reserved empty grassy plot next to the fields for future expansion.

Paths connect every production building to the central stockpile and link housing to workplaces. A handful of tiny citizens and one handcart may illustrate automatic labor. No smelter, no metal mine tunnel, no electric power, no motors, no army. All facilities directly serve food, housing or tool technology. The bay, forest and hill stay in their original places.

STAGE 4: ELECTRIC INDUSTRY AND VEHICLE PRODUCTION, a later single-planet civilization stage. Retain the same forest reserve at upper left with an upgraded sawmill at its edge, the rocky resource hill at upper right, the calm lower-left bay, and recognizable older districts. Upgrade the compact north-central housing cluster in place to six modest low-rise brick apartment/workers houses. Keep three productive agricultural plots and a granary in the lower-left/center inland area, with a short shallow plain-blue irrigation ditch if it fits the established terrain. There are still forest resources, food production and small open grass areas; industry must not erase the economy that supports it.

Arrange a distinct purposeful INDUSTRIAL CORRIDOR on the right hemisphere: the ore mine remains at the hill foot; a brick smelter below it produces clearly visible stacked steel ingots; a machine-parts workshop below the smelter has gears and crates outside; a vehicle assembly hall farther down on the lower-right buildable area has a wide open assembly bay and an unfinished chassis visible inside. Each facility is separated by a short section of road and clearly identifiable by its work in progress.

Place ONE modest electricity GENERATOR STATION adjacent to the industrial zone with two small turbine housings, a transformer and a single restrained smokestack. A short, tidy run of three simple power poles connects the generator to the factory buildings. Do not cover the planet in cables. Two small low-poly trucks carry resources along the actual industrial road.

Immediately adjacent to the vehicle assembly hall, include a compact functional VEHICLE MUSTER YARD containing EXACTLY TWO small clearly readable olive-green tracked tanks and one low barracks/service shed. Tanks are the manufactured output and a managed squad, not decorative units sprinkled over the landscape; do not stage any battle. This military production competes for parts and electricity. Central storage upgrades in place into an organized warehouse with food crates, timber and metal stocks. A small research/engineering annex belongs to the machine workshop. No arbitrary castles, no residential skyscrapers, no airport, no rockets, no spacecraft, no extra planet.

Maintain low-poly game-ready forms and legible economic relationships: farms sustain population, resource sites feed industry, generator supplies factories, assembly produces trucks and tanks. Show concentrated districts and a coherent hierarchy instead of a random dense city. Keep the coastline and water simple and consistent with the reference.
